clue.text: Lady promoting European dairy product

indicators.note: in a down entry, promoting the European letter means lifting it from the bottom of the word to the top

blocks.note: a dame is a titled lady

explanation.surface: A woman is out marketing some continental cheese or yoghurt.
explanation.walkthrough: DAME has its final E (the usual abbreviation for European) moved up to the top of the down entry, giving EDAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese, and cheese is a product of the dairy.

clue.text: Ring about one to get engineers round around third of July

indicators.note: third of tells us to keep only the letter in third position of the following word
round says the engineers go about the outside of what follows, enclosing it

blocks.note: c. (circa) means about
the Roman numeral for one
Royal Engineers
c. (circa) again, meaning around
the third letter of July

explanation.surface: Someone tries to ring round some engineers in early July.
explanation.walkthrough: C (about) and I (one) come first; then RE (Royal Engineers) wraps around C (around again) plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle and a ring are both a closed round shape, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Directors seen with Catholic barbers?

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Catholic
a whimsical coinage: barbers are men who deal with hair

explanation.surface: Company directors are spotted in the company of Catholic hairdressers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word: barbers as 'hair men'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chairmen preside over company boards, making them the senior directors of a firm.

clue.text: Vacuous babysitter Hoskins is giving lip

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied out, so the inside of the word is removed and only its two ends remain

blocks.note: the outside letters of babysitter
Hoskins is the setter, so 'Hoskins is' becomes I'M

explanation.surface: A dim-witted babysitter called Hoskins is being cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters refer to themselves by their pen-name, so 'Hoskins is' is 'I am', I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: The brim of a cup or bowl is its rim or edge, which can also be called its lip.

clue.text: Charlie breaking wind has ruined lunchtime snack

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into the middle of the following words, so the letter goes inside them
something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie broke wind and spoilt everyone's lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' does double service here: it is part of the anagram fodder 'wind has', and there is no separate link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandwich is a classic light lunch, filling between two slices of bread.

clue.text: Example of one of many here beggar randomly hugs

definitions.text: Example of one of many here

indicators.note: the phrase hugs the target, holding it inside its run of letters across the word boundary

blocks.note: the letters sit across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A random beggar embraces one of a crowd of people.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid is full of islands (Harris, Capri, Man, Midway, Madeira, Canary and more), so 'one of many here' is an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Arran is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde, one example of the many isles in this grid's theme.

clue.text: Dance with a famous American artist

blocks.note: a hop is an informal dance
a, as in 'ten pounds a head', means per

explanation.surface: Someone dances with a celebrated painter from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Hopper was the American painter of Nighthawks, a famous realist artist.

clue.text: Bomber has to circle river near Rhode Island

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it, so these letters wrap around what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river
the US state's postal abbreviation

explanation.surface: A bomber plane has to circle a river close to the American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bomber' Harris was the RAF commander of Bomber Command in the Second World War; Harris is also a Hebridean island, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Harris was nicknamed Bomber for leading the RAF's strategic bombing campaign.

clue.text: One working with Scotsmen and old Greeks

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a machine that is working is on
Ian is a typically Scottish name, so Scotsmen are Ians

explanation.surface: Someone works alongside Scots and ancient Greeks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionians were one of the main tribes of ancient Greece, settled in Ionia and Attica.

clue.text: One beaten with sticks initially lost spirit

indicators.note: initially lost means the opening letter has gone missing

blocks.note: a drum is struck with drumsticks

explanation.surface: Someone who has been thrashed with sticks has lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is also a small Hebridean island, in keeping with the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a distilled alcoholic drink, and spirit is the general word for such liquor.

clue.text: Beat foremost of racers to get to No.1 in this?

definitions.text: Beat foremost of racers to get to No.1 in this?

indicators.note: foremost means the very front, so only the leading letter is kept

blocks.note: to cap something is to top or outdo it
the first letter of racers
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A driver hopes to overtake the leading racers and finish first in this car.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the Ford Capri, a sporty 1970s coupé one might race in; Capri is also the Italian island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford Capri was a sporty coupé, the kind of car someone might imagine racing to victory in.

clue.text: Guy in Maiden seen by rest room taking cocaine

indicators.note: taking here means taking away, so a letter is removed from the room

blocks.note: M is the cricket scorer's symbol for a maiden over
the can is American slang for a toilet
C is drug slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A member of Iron Maiden is spotted by the toilets snorting cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' looks like consuming, but here it removes C from CAN; in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs. Man is also the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy and man are both everyday informal words for an adult male person.

clue.text: A bit like a mankini, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: a single portion or fragment
second meaning: describing a garment made as a single whole

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests something slightly resembling a mankini; read separately, 'a bit' is a single portion and a mankini is an all-in-one garment.
explanation.definitionFit: One piece is a single fragment, and one-piece describes swimwear made in a single unit, as the mankini is.

clue.text: A prime example of pressure on aristocrat

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A first-rate case of pressure being put on a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'P on EARL' places P above EARL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is something precious and choice, so the finest specimen of its kind is called a pearl.

clue.text: Militant leader: "I'd swerve back towards the centre"

indicators.note: the leader is whatever comes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept
back tells us to read the swerving word from its end to its start

blocks.note: the first letter of Militant
taken as written, without the apostrophe
to yaw is to swerve off course

explanation.surface: A militant figurehead says they would swing back towards the political centre ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Midway is also a Pacific atoll, scene of the 1942 battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Midway means halfway between two points, i.e. at or towards the middle.

clue.text: Daughter gets pop, but not British rap/metal singer

indicators.note: but not says the following item is excluded from the word before it

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
to pop a balloon is to burst it
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A daughter gets into pop music, but not the British kind, preferring a rap-metal singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Durst fronts Limp Bizkit, the American nu-metal band blending rap vocals with metal.

clue.text: Hoskins goes to a party with grass producer

blocks.note: Hoskins is the setter, who refers to themself as me
taken as written
a do is a party
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: The setter heads to a party with someone who supplies marijuana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass producer' looks like a drug dealer, but it is a field where grass grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a field of grass grown for hay, so it literally produces grass.

clue.text: Booze manufactured by old revolutionaries

blocks.note: something manufactured has been made
the Irish Republican Army, an old revolutionary force

explanation.surface: Alcohol brewed by former rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: Madeira is also a Portuguese island in the Atlantic, which gave the wine its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine, and booze is informal for any alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Bet loose pants will be unfashionable

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are in a poor state and must be reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wagering that baggy trousers will go out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' reads as trousers (or loose underwear), but in British slang it means rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete means out of date and no longer used, close to unfashionable.

clue.text: Ancient Greek city with half-completed rosery

indicators.note: only half completed means just the opening half of the word has been written

blocks.note: and means with or plus
the first three of its six letters

explanation.surface: An old Greek town comes with a rose garden still under construction.
explanation.walkthrough: A rosery is a rose garden. Andros is also an island in the Cyclades.
explanation.definitionFit: Andros was the ancient city on the Greek island of the same name in the Aegean.

clue.text: One providing relief around tense religious festival

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first item wraps around the next

blocks.note: one that eases pain
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone brings comfort during a stressful religious holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Easter Island in the Pacific fits the theme of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian feast celebrating the resurrection of Jesus.

clue.text: Theologian tucking into beers becomes muddled

indicators.note: tucking into means getting stuck inside, so the first item goes within the second

blocks.note: ales are beers
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A theologian drinking beers gets confused.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to confuse, so something that addles is turning muddled.

clue.text: Old can of talc Zara chucked all over the place

indicators.note: items chucked all over the place are scattered at random, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old tin of talcum powder that Zara threw everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a tin, but it is slang for prison; Alcatraz is the former island prison in San Francisco Bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang for jail, and Alcatraz was a notorious prison closed in 1963.

clue.text: Is it possible out-of-head Gary will get grass?

indicators.note: out of head means the head, or first letter, is put out of the name

blocks.note: can as in 'can it be?'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Can a stoned Gary get hold of some marijuana?
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' and 'out-of-head' suggest drugs; a grass is also an informer, and so is a canary, since it 'sings' to police. The Canary Islands fit the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Both grass and canary are slang for an informer who sings, telling the police what they know.

clue.text: Passage 25, after adding punctuation, is to be read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud means we are to go by the sound when spoken rather than the spelling

blocks.note: the answer to 25 across with an apostrophe inserted becomes the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: A passage from a text is to be read out once commas and full stops are added.
explanation.walkthrough: The 25 answer gains an apostrophe to become I'LL, which is pronounced exactly like the answer; it also sounds like isle, nodding to the island theme.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats, as in a church or aeroplane.

clue.text: Tablet having no power could create trouble

indicators.note: having no means the named letter is absent from the word

blocks.note: a pill is a tablet
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A pill that doesn't work could bring on problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill as a noun means harm or misfortune, as in 'the ills of society', which is trouble.

clue.text: Pork pie stuffed with bit of nougat's rank

indicators.note: just a bit of the word means a single letter, its first, is taken
stuffed with means filled with, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: rhyming slang: pork pie means lie
the first letter of nougat

explanation.surface: A pork pie filled with a piece of nougat smells foul.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie. 'rank' looks like an adjective (foul-smelling) but is a noun, a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank of soldiers is a line of them standing side by side.

clue.text: After a change of heart, rabbit in French language

indicators.note: a change of heart means the middle letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: lapin is French for rabbit

explanation.surface: Someone changes their mind and chatters away in French.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle P of LAPIN is replaced by T; 'rabbit' also means talk, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the language of ancient Rome, ancestor of French.

clue.text: Function of Starmer? Primarily to go after Conservative!

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letter of each word is taken
to go after places these letters behind the next item

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: What role does Keir Starmer play? Mainly to chase the Tories!
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer is the Labour leader, so chasing the Conservatives is his job; Cos (Kos) is also a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is the abbreviation for cosine, a trigonometric function in mathematics.

clue.text: Doctor, chef or captain?

blocks.note: first meaning: to falsify, as in tampering with the accounts
second meaning: a person who prepares food
third meaning: the 18th-century British naval explorer of the Pacific

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: to doctor figures is to cook them, a chef is a cook, and Captain James Cook explored the Pacific, where the Cook Islands carry his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cook means to falsify figures (doctor), a person who makes meals (chef), and the explorer Captain James Cook.

clue.text: One that will flap and go on about new film

blocks.note: gan is the Scots and Northern English dialect word for go
N is the abbreviation for new
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.surface: Someone who panics and keeps going on about a new film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flap' suggests getting in a panic, but it is the beating of wings; 'on about' merely joins the pieces, a loose touch.
explanation.definitionFit: The gannet is a large seabird, and a bird is something that flaps its wings.

clue.text: Order foe to get changed given make-over by Thatcher?

indicators.note: changed means altered in form, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An enemy is told to change, reformed in the style of Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thatcher' reads as the former Prime Minister, but it is a tradesperson who roofs with straw or reed.
explanation.definitionFit: A thatcher puts on roofs of straw, so a house redone by one has been given a new roof.
